new_issues.description: Appendix B attributes RT-CGM's excess collinear fraction (0.305 against at most 0.229 for admitted cohorts) 'mainly' to runs of identical readings, but no versioned record decomposes the statistic into flat and sloped triples (diadata_audit_r1.json reports only the aggregate fraction, and experiments/audit_diadata.py computes only the aggregate), and the sentence does not consider that runs of identical readings on a five-minute grid can themselves be a resampling (sample-and-hold) signature for devices of a different native cadence, which would bias rate labels toward stable in round five's primary-endpoint cohort.

dissents.original_operationalization: [routed: EIC / Journal-Fit Reviewer, card #1] A cohort table exists, and every cohort named in the abstract, sections 7.10-7.13 or Table 1 has a row stating its role (e.g., training, calibration pool, held-out, confirmatory, probe) and its CGM sensor model/generation, with mixed or unrecoverable devices marked as such (Round-1 audit record: RT-CGM = JDRF CGM RCT with DexCom SEVEN, MiniMed Paradigm and FreeStyle Navigator, per-subject sensor not recoverable). Round-1 known names to check include Weinstock, CITY, DLCP3, REPLACE-BG, SENCE, WISDM, RT-CGM, PEDAP, dubosson and hall, plus any other cohort named on those surfaces. Check by enumerating cohort names on the four surfaces and matching rows. The Requirement's further columns (source trial and citation, n, age range, diabetes type, therapy, blinded or real-time wear, collection years, reportable range) and an RT-CGM device/era description in sections 7.11 and 10.2 are consistent with, but not required by, this criterion.
dissents.replacement_operationalization: Identical to the original, except that 'every cohort named in ... Table 1' is read as every cohort this work itself uses that is named in Table 1 (the GlucoEdge row, plus any cohort the manuscript trains, calibrates, selects or evaluates on). A dataset named in Table 1 only as a prior study's evaluation scope (OhioT1DM in the Mirshekarian and Martinsson rows; Zhu et al.'s 'three clinical datasets') needs no cohort-table row. All other conditions apply unchanged: role and CGM sensor model/generation per row, mixed or unrecoverable devices marked, and RT-CGM consistent with the Round-1 audit record.
dissents.evidence: A literal reading would require a cohort-table row for OhioT1DM. The revised Table 1 names it (L272-273), as the original did (original_main.tex L206-207), only as the evaluation scope of Mirshekarian et al. and Martinsson et al.; this work never uses it. The Round-1 Requirement for this item asks for 'a cohort table for every GlucoBench and DiaData cohort used', and its problem statement concerns the cohorts behind the shipped model. Phase 1's own list of known names (Weinstock, CITY, DLCP3, REPLACE-BG, SENCE, WISDM, RT-CGM, PEDAP, dubosson, hall) leaves out OhioT1DM even though it appeared in Round-1 Table 1, which indicates that prior-work rows were not meant to count.
dissents.decision_impact_note: Under the original literal criterion the verdict would be PARTIALLY_ADDRESSED, with one gap: no cohort-table row for OhioT1DM, a residual this seat would grade consider. Under the replacement it is FULLY_ADDRESSED, because every cohort this work uses that is named in the Abstract, Round-1 §7.10-§7.13 (now §8.3-§8.6) or Table 1 has a row with role and sensor generation. Because this dissent is on a must_fix item, it trips the independent-adjudication bound.
